headline: Florida's Leatherback Turtles Set Record for Second Year Running
meta_description: Leatherback turtles in Florida are on track for a second consecutive nesting record in 2026, with over 2,200 nests already documented.
summary_short: Florida's leatherback turtles are thriving. With 2,209 nests already recorded in 2026, they're poised to break last year's record of 2,012 nests.
body:
Florida's leatherback turtles are on track to break their own nesting record for the second consecutive year. As of now in 2026, 2,209 nests have already been documented—surpassing the previous record of 2,012 nests set in 2025.

The surge in nesting activity offers a rare bright spot in conservation efforts. Leatherback sea turtles, the largest living turtle species, have faced decades of decline due to ocean pollution, fishing nets, and habitat loss. The back-to-back record years in Florida suggest that recent protective measures and beach restoration efforts may finally be paying off.

Loggerhead turtles have also seen improvements, though the available data remains incomplete. Still, the momentum building across Florida's nesting beaches signals hope for these ancient mariners navigating an increasingly challenging ocean.
quick_facts: 2,209 leatherback nests documented in Florida in 2026
Previous record of 2,012 nests set in 2025
